page.layout: One page of text in one main column; a narrow block of marginal notes cut off at the left edge of the scan (partly visible, fragmentary, from the facing page, not transcribed as notes); a small mark "5" beside the right margin at the line "Alios tropos". Running head at top; page number at top right.

main_text.p: sensiles actiones, cum pane & vino proprie fiunt, corpori & sanguini, quæ nimirum nostris sensibus minime obnoxia sunt, tribui propter sacramentalem unionem, juxta synecdoches illas: Johannes vidit Spiritum sanctum. Moses vidit audivitque Deum facie ad faciem. Nec adversatur aut repugnat admodum. Petrus Viretus dicto superius loco cap.17. & 18. huic sententiæ: quin ii ò synecdochen eam amicè cum metonymia conciliat, ut videbitur inferius. Et ita Gualtherus in præfatione Homiliarum in Matthæum: Ideò autem inquit hæc dico, ut ostendam vos, ut ut clametis verba Christi clara, simplicia & perspicua esse, effugere non posse tropum omnem, quin Metonymiam aut Synecdochen admittere cogamini. Quo argumento docet, non esse synecdochen nostræ doctrinæ adversam & contrariam.

Alios tropos & nominant & numerant Theologi. Ita namque placet aliis Theologis metonymiam nominare tropum, quo explicatur doctrina Eucharistica. Ita Danæus respon. ad Laonicam Spongiam ad partem secun-dam: Christum ipsum, inquit, etiam quatenus homo est, affirmamus piis in sua cœna vere quidem, sed non corporalis præsentiæ modo adesse: panem autem illum & vinum illud

page.notes: Marginal notes on the left edge are cut off and unreadable. The printed word "Alios" and the numeral "5" at the right margin are the only marginal marks. Some words in the top lines are partly obscured by stains (e.g. "ii ò", "Laonicam"); the reading "Laonicam" and "Spongiam" follow the scan and may be doubtful. The word "nominant" is followed by a gap in the scan where "&" appears to be printed.
